The cannabis family was measured at 23 rows carrying 415 English names, and the ONLY 4 recipe lines it ever answered were the cannabis row holding 'flour', removed already. These 22 rows carry ZERO recipe lines between them. Measured before removal: 659 distinct names, 649 of which become unreachable and 10 of which stay answerable on a surviving row. The 271 English names that lose their only home are strain names (Bubba Kush, Purple Haze), preparation names (Space cake, Weed brownie, THC gummies) and article titles about legality (Cannabis in Japan, Adverse effects of medical cannabis). None is food vocabulary. ⚠️ hashish also held 'overhead costs', 'real costs' and 'shadow prices'. Catalan slang 'costo' for hashish normalizes onto AGROVOC c_1922 'Costo', the Spanish prefLabel for the ECONOMICS concept costs. That is the fourth cross-language homograph traced in this pipeline, after ni/nickel, gula/sugar and Slovene moka putting Turkish coffee on flour.
